gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each under-$100 three-channel camera costs once parking power and GPS are added: the Redtiger A3 goes from $72.74 to $108.73 with Redtiger's $35.99 hardwire kit, and the Vantrue OnDash N4 from $99.99 to $129.98 with Vantrue's $29.99 kit and $151.97 with its $21.99 GPS mount, while the 70mai T800E's $93.99 Amazon listing names GPS and a 64 GB card in the title.
standout_why: Compared against deal.ai (12 priced picks), my-best (8 tested 3-channel cams), cabincommand, offkeytikki, productbible, dashanddrive, roadgearlab, redlinecargarage and the cited Digital Camera World page. Deal.ai already carries the two headline prices (N4 $99.99, A3 $72.74), so price alone is only part-new. None of them prices a hardwire kit or GPS mount for any 3-channel camera; productbible gives only a generic '$18 to $50 more' for 1- and 2-channel cams. None states the N4's all-three-recording mode: deal.ai titles it '3-Channel 4K' without mapping channels. Digital Camera World's visible text names no 3-channel camera, and the cited Walmart page returned a robot check.
decides: It confirms a three-way split among the named brands at or under $100 on 2026-11-26, and puts a camera we link in that top three. The Redtiger A3 ($72.74) wins on price with Wi-Fi and a supercapacitor. The 70mai T800E ($93.99, Amazon) wins on what the title says is included: GPS, Wi-Fi 6 and a 64 GB card. The Vantrue OnDash N4 ($99.99, our link) is the only one with a maker-named sensor (Sony STARVIS) and a named test: my-best read plates 'in both good and bad conditions'. The N4 loses on extras: GPS is a separate $21.99 mount, my-best says it has no app, and $99.99 is a sale price against a $259.99 compare-at. No camera here stays under $100 once a parking kit is added, so the page should say the budget covers driving recording only. The page need not skip.
